essayTitle: Technology Alone Cannot Save Our Planet
source: Perlis 2026 · Paper 2 · Part 3 Q4 · Article, 200–250 words
paragraphs: Environmental problems are getting worse every year. While technology offers promising solutions, I believe it cannot save our planet without changes in human behaviour.

One environmental problem faced today is plastic pollution. Millions of tonnes of plastic waste end up in our oceans every year, choking marine life and contaminating the food chain. Even our own beaches in Perlis are often littered with plastic bottles after the monsoon season.

This problem is happening mainly because of our throwaway culture. Many people use single-use plastics for convenience and discard them after just a few minutes. Furthermore, poor waste management systems worsen the situation. In many areas, rubbish is not properly collected or recycled, so it often ends up in rivers and seas.

Technology can help solve environmental problems by creating eco-friendly alternatives. For example, scientists have developed biodegradable packaging made from plant materials that decomposes within months. Moreover, smart recycling machines can make waste management more efficient. Some machines even reward users with points for every bottle they recycle, encouraging good habits.
In conclusion, technology is a powerful tool, but it is not a magic wand. Only when innovation goes hand in hand with responsible behaviour can we truly protect our planet for generations to come.
